summary: Yakima County, WA lookout first used in 1920; 55 ft wooden tower (1935), 60 ft steel tower (1942) removed after 1979; Yakama land, permission needed.

facts.design: First used 1920 with a limber pole tower and cabin; 3-legged 55 ft wooden tower with 8x8 ft cab (1935); 60 ft Aermotor steel tower (1942)
facts.status_note: Steel tower removed after 1979 per Willhite; the register says the site has since been removed; only undated photo captions of footings describe the site

access.note: Willhite: on Yakama Nation land and access is forbidden without special permission. TrailChick: most of the reservation is closed to non-tribal members

visit.drive_up: Willhite says a 4WD vehicle is needed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Willhite dates removal of the steel tower to after 1979. The register says only that it has since been removed, and FireLookout's heading leaves the 1942 tower's end open with '1942-?'. The story gives Willhite's date and notes the open end.

The register names the Yakima Indian Reservation as administrator, Willhite calls the land Yakama Nation land, and Forest Lookouts uses Yakima Indian Agency. These name the same land and are not treated as a factual conflict; the record keeps the register's name.

notes_for_editor: Brief elevation 1953.8 m matches FFLOS 6,410 ft. No source describes the site as it stands now; the Willhite footing captions are undated, so the story does not say the site is unchanged. Access was not checked on the ground and rests on Willhite and a trip blog. The TrailChick page is a trip blog, not an official statement. No photo URLs were captured.
